To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chiral effective theory provides a convergent expansion of the NN potential and the deuteron charge form factors, that the NN potential can be calculated with a precision that is limited only by our ignorance of the NN contact terms, that the deuteron charge operators can be calculated with an accuracy that is limited only our ignorance of the deuteron form factors, and that the deuteron wave functions can be calculated with the precision of chiral effective theory and the accuracy of the deuteron charge and form factors.
the nucleon-nucleon system in nuclear physics can be studied with chiral perturbation techniques, that this is a reliable method, and that it is a good way to study the nuclear force.

the chiral expansion for the NN potential converges slowly and that it is not possible to use it to calculate NN scattering phase shifts with an accuracy that is better than 1% or so for QCD coupling constants of the order of the QCD scale.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a systematic approach to the description of the NN system.
a systematic expansion of the nucleon‐nuclear force in terms of the pion mass.
the development of the chiral perturbation expansion as a tool to study the nucleon‐nuclear system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the NN interaction is a well‐understood system in which the low‐energy effective theory is applicable, and in which the low energy constants of the effective theory have been fixed with a high level of confidence.
chiral EFT provides a very useful framework for studying the nucleon‐nuclear system.
the chiral expansion of the nucleon-nucleon interaction is convergent and that it provides an accurate representation of low-energy nucleon-nucleons dynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NN potential and the deuteron charge form factors can be computed in chiral effective field theory, and the results agree with the experimental data.
chiral effective field theory is a useful tool to describe the nucleon‐nuclear interaction at low energies.

the NN potential and charge operators in chiral effective field theory have been shown to be convergent and to give reliable results for NN phase shifts, deuteron charge form factors and deuteron binding energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chiral perturbation can be applied to the NN system with confidence.
the convergence properties of chiral effective field theory are very sensitive to the regularization procedure used in the calculation of the two‐nucleon force.
chiral perturbation theories can be used to predict low energy NN scattering observables with good precision.
